snippet.title: Michael DiLeonardo: The Story of a Gambino Family Member and His Testimony | Gangster Sleep Story
snippet.description:
Michael “Mikey Scars” DiLeonardo, born in 1955 in Brooklyn, New York, represents one of the most dramatic and consequential transformations in modern Mafia history. Raised in the close-knit world of Bensonhurst, he rose from street-level associate to a powerful captain in the Gambino crime family. Once trusted with business operations, political connections, and top-level strategy, DiLeonardo became one of the organization’s most influential members during the Gotti era.

But his story was also one of loyalty stretched to breaking. As the Gambino family descended into internal conflict and federal pressure mounted, DiLeonardo faced a choice that would change the course of Mafia history. Arrested in the early 2000s and charged with racketeering and extortion, DiLeonardo found himself fighting not only the government — but the organization he had devoted his life to.

Abandoned financially by the family he helped build, DiLeonardo made a decision almost unheard of at his level: he cooperated with the federal government. His testimony became one of the most important insider accounts of the American Mafia in the 21st century. From union rackets to secret meetings, he unveiled the modern structure of Cosa Nostra and helped secure major convictions.

His story is a rare window into a world usually sealed by silence — and a reflection on loyalty, betrayal, and the cost of power.

• The inner politics of the Gotti era and the changes in modern Mafia operations

snippet.title: Joseph “The Animal” Barboza: The Deadliest Hitman in Boston Mob History | Gangster Sleep Story
snippet.description:
Joseph “The Animal” Barboza, born in 1932 in New Bedford, Massachusetts, was one of the most feared and violent figures in the history of Boston’s criminal underworld. Known for his uncontrollable temper and ruthless efficiency, Barboza built a reputation as a contract killer long before most men ever earned a nickname. In a city already defined by corruption and bloodshed, he stood out as something even darker — a man whose violence had no limits.

Barboza operated within the shadowy world of the Winter Hill Gang, working alongside figures like Raymond Patriarca, Stephen Flemmi, and Whitey Bulger. His loyalty was transactional, his methods brutal. Bodies piled up quietly, often without witnesses, as Barboza enforced mob discipline with chilling precision. But violence alone was never enough to protect him.

When federal pressure closed in, Barboza made a decision that shocked the underworld — he became a government witness. His testimony exposed a vast web of corruption linking organized crime to police, judges, and politicians across New England. In doing so, he helped dismantle parts of the Boston mob — but also sealed his own fate. Forced into witness protection, Barboza lived the rest of his life hunted by the very world he helped reveal.

His story is a haunting reminder of how violence breeds betrayal — and how the line between hunter and hunted can vanish overnight.

• The murders that earned him the nickname “The Animal”

snippet.title: How Illegal Pain Clinics Actually Work | How Crime Works | Insider
snippet.description:
Jason Votrobek was convicted in 2014 on drug trafficking and money-laundering charges and later sentenced to 15 years in federal prison.

Votrobek talks to Business Insider about his early days smuggling cocaine and his role in the prescription opioid trade. Votrobek co-owned and operated Atlanta Medical Group, a Georgia clinic that distributed large volumes of oxycodone and other prescription drugs.

He describes how pain clinics capitalized on the demand for prescription opioids.  Lawsuits against companies like Purdue Pharma, the maker of OxyContin, led to several changes in the system. Purdue and its owners agreed to pay up to $6 billion in a settlement tied to claims over their role in the opioid epidemic.

Although the "pill mill" era peaked in the early 2010s, the consequences persist. More than 107,000 Americans died from drug overdoses in 2023, with opioids, particularly fentanyl, responsible for the majority of those deaths.

Editor's Note: A previous version of this video incorrectly stated that Purdue Pharma created Oxycodone. The video has been corrected at 44:08 to clarify that Purdue Pharma created the prescription painkiller OxyContin. OxyContin is a slow release form of Oxycodone.

He survived a nail bomb. He survived eight shotgun blasts at point-blank range. But he couldn't survive a handshake from the man he called "Father."
On September 14, 1984, the body of 28-year-old Salvatore "Salvie" Testa was found dumped on a secluded New Jersey road. He was dressed in tennis shorts and a T-shirt, executed with two bullets to the back of the head. To the public, he was just another mob casualty. To the underworld, he was the "Crown Prince" of Philadelphia—the most feared, loyal, and charismatic hitman the city had ever seen.

In this video, we go inside the violent collapse of the Philadelphia Crime Family. We trace the line from the assassination of the "Gentle Don" Angelo Bruno to the explosive death of "The Chicken Man" Philip Testa, and finally to the paranoid reign of Nicodemo "Little Nicky" Scarfo.
This is a story of Shakespearean betrayal: How a young man who served his boss with absolute loyalty was murdered not for his failures, but for his success.

Berke became the first operational pilot qualified in the F-35B Lightning II. He flew the F/A-18 Hornet, as well as several other fighter jets, served as a forward air controller on the ground in Iraq, and later became an instructor at TOPGUN.

Berke speaks with Business Insider about the realities of operating as a pilot aboard an aircraft carrier, including the demands of carrier life and combat deployments following 9/11.

In 2026 alone, US aircraft carriers participated in combat missions in Venezuela, Iran, and Yemen.

Since retiring as lieutenant colonel from the Marine Corps in 2017, Berke has worked as an instructor and executive at Echelon Front, where he teaches leadership, accountability, and decision-making under pressure.

snippet.title: How 6 Secretive Government Roles Actually Work — from CIA Black Ops to The FBI | Marathon
snippet.description:
Joaquín "Jack" García is a retired FBI agent who spent 24 of his 26 years working undercover. He infiltrated the Gambino crime family for three years under the alias "Jack Falcone," even attending a self-described "mob school" to learn its culture and habits. His close relationship with caporegime Greg DePalma helped lead to the indictment of 32 mobsters. Since retiring in 2006, he has written the New York Times bestseller "Making Jack Falcone."

John Kiriakou is a former CIA officer who specialized in counterterrorism and was chief of operations in Pakistan in 2002. He later became one of the first whistleblowers to speak publicly about the CIA's torture program. After leaving the agency, he transitioned into media and consulting work. Kiriakou has written several books about his experiences and now hosts weekly podcasts. His career reflects both insider knowledge and public criticism of intelligence practices.

FBI agent Scott Payne spent decades targeting violent extremist groups, including neo-Nazi cells, the KKK, and outlaw biker gangs. He began his career in South Carolina before joining the FBI in 1998, working across multiple field offices on drug trafficking, human trafficking, and domestic terrorism. Payne went undercover with the Outlaws Motorcycle Club and later helped stop planned attacks, including a synagogue plot and a mass shooting linked to The Base. Since leaving the bureau in 2021, he has become a speaker and author of Code Name: Pale Horse.

Kenneth Valentine served as a US Secret Service agent for 24 years, protecting Presidents Bill Clinton, George W. Bush, and Barack Obama. His career placed him at the center of some of the most sensitive security operations in the country. Valentine has offered insight into recent assassination attempts on Donald Trump and what they reveal about systemic vulnerabilities. Today, he works as an author, leadership expert, and public speaker.

Andrew Bustamante spent seven years as a covert CIA officer after being recruited while applying to the Peace Corps. A former US Air Force serviceman, he gained deep insight into intelligence operations and claims to have coordinated drone strikes in Iraq and Afghanistan. He also emphasizes the importance of deception as a core espionage skill. Today, he runs EverydaySpy, a company that teaches intelligence techniques to the general public.

Mickey Bergman is a negotiator who works to secure the release of Americans wrongfully detained abroad. Over the past decade, he has helped free high-profile detainees including Trevor Reed, Brittney Griner, and Danny Fenster. Operating independently of governments, he travels into hostile regions to negotiate directly with captors. His approach, which he calls “fringe diplomacy,” prioritizes emotional intelligence over force.
